method.class: statistics-only log-scale regression predictor of random-walk cover time on small graphs
method.description: On evaluator-synthesized connected graphs with 5 <= n <= 30 from ten declared families, a predictor that sees only six cheap statistics (n, m, mean degree, max degree, min degree, diameter) and is fitted on evaluator Monte Carlo labels predicts the uniform-start expected cover time on isomorphism-disjoint held-out graphs with lower mean absolute log-ratio error than the generic upper bounds 2m(n-1) and (4/27)n^3 used as predictors, with per-family errors identifying where it is reliable or fails, and Monte Carlo plus graph-sampling bootstrap uncertainty reported. The claim is limited to these families, sizes and target definition; the predictor is not an upper bound. Candidate operations: reset -> fit(training statistics, Monte Carlo labels, standard errors) -> three predict calls over held-out statistics; only the six statistics (n, m, mean degree, max degree, min degree, diameter) are candidate-visible for held-out graphs.

artifacts.source: Authored by the draft agent: non-secret data/label seeds, pool sizes and walk counts for the shared training pool and search eval pool; graphs and labels are synthesized deterministically by evaluate.py.
Authored by the draft agent: training/search-eval seeds (for regeneration and dedup) plus privileged final eval data/label seeds, episode salt and bootstrap seed; consumed only by evaluate_final.py.

baselines: aklrr_2m(n-1): Aleliunas et al. 1979 generic cover-time upper bound 2m(n-1) used as a point predictor
feige_lead_(4/27)n^3: leading term of Feige 1995 generic upper bound, leading-order only
best_bound: per-graph min(2m(n-1), (4/27)n^3), primary comparator for the research question
matthews_ref: max_{u,v} H(u,v) * H_{n-1} from exact hitting times on the full adjacency (graph-specific reference, not statistics-only, not a claim comparator)
ols_ref: evaluator OLS of ln C on [1, ln n, ln m] fitted on the shared training pool (ridge 1e-8)
constant_control: geometric mean of training labels for every eval graph (negative control)

permuted_feature_control: evaluator-private derangement re-pairing eval rows with other graphs' features (moves every row, changes >=80% of feature vectors, redrawn up to 100 times; vacuous control blocks correctness)
reordered_copy_control: same eval rows in a different private order; predictions must match main within relative 1e-6
starter_program_0: ridge log-linear regression on log statistics (program_0/src/program.py)
protocol.promotion_rule: Search eligibility (search correct=true) requires only validity/integrity gates with no comparative threshold: simulator closed-form checks pass, all baselines finite, zero isomorphism overlap between training and search eval pools, every declared episode completes reset/fit/3x predict with schema-valid responses, all main predictions finite and positive, predictions reproduce within relative 1e-6 across the main call, the reordered-copy control and the permuted-feature control rows (pure function of the six statistics), the permuted-feature control is non-vacuous, and predictions are not constant across rows with distinct features. Eligible candidates are ranked by combined_score = -(main mean absolute log-ratio error; graph->family->episode->plane equal weights) descending; ties within 1e-12 broken by lower max per-family search error, then earlier submission. The single evaluated candidate of the 1x1 campaign is frozen if eligible, with its program_0/src digest recorded before final seeds or pools are revealed; if ineligible no final claim is made. Final validity (final correct=true) applies the same gates on final seeds [211,212,213] plus zero isomorphism overlap across training, search eval and final eval pools. Claim assessment is separate from validity: 'more accurate than generic upper bounds' is supported only if final correct=true and delta_vs_best_bound_ci_high < 0; per-family deltas with CIs straddling 0 are 'not distinguishable', family error > ln 2 is 'fails: off by more than 2x'; feature reliance is claimed only if delta_permuted_minus_main_ci_low > 0. Beating the bounds is not a search veto.

search_proxies.name: search_eval_pool_proxy
search_proxies.preserves: Same ten graph families (path, cycle, star, complete, grid, binary_tree, lollipop, random_tree, erdos_renyi, random_regular3), 5<=n<=30, six evaluator-computed statistics, uniform-start Monte Carlo cover-time target with R=256 walks, shared training pool, reset/fit/3x predict transcript, per-graph log-ratio error capped at ln 1000, equal-weight graph->family->episode->plane aggregation, identical baselines and negative controls, identical integrity gates.
search_proxies.omits: Final eval graphs (deterministic shapes with n mod 3 == 2 and grid shapes at round-robin index 2, random graphs from privileged final data seeds), the larger final eval pool (~116 vs ~86 graphs, 16 vs 8 per random family), the third episode, the paired two-level bootstrap CIs, per-family deltas versus the best bound, and the final claim assessment.

search_visible: Shared training pool features, Monte Carlo cover-time labels, label standard errors and walk counts (delivered via the fit RPC).
Search eval pool features (via predict RPC), without labels, in evaluator-private orders.

Search metrics.json scalars: combined_score, main and per-family errors, baseline and control errors, order-invariance diff, failed_episodes, MC relative SE median, capped walks, isomorphism-overlap and feature-collision counts; search correct.json.
Bounded search-only failure categories (component, category, operation) on stderr and starter candidate code in program_0/src.
final_sealed: Final eval pool graphs, their Monte Carlo labels and final data-generation seeds.
Final reset seeds [211,212,213] until candidate freeze, and final smoke outputs.
Final metrics.json, per-family final errors, bootstrap CIs and claim assessment outcomes.
Evaluator-private control permutations and row orderings.

required_evidence: canonical task.md SHA-256 and frozen candidate program_0/src digest recorded before final pools/seeds were revealed.
Split manifest: generator parameters, data seeds, source IDs, WL-hash plus VF2 isomorphism check showing zero overlap across training, search eval and final eval; feature-collision count.
Simulator validation table versus closed forms (cycle, complete graph, path) with standard errors, and count of capped walks.

Final main table: candidate, AKLRR 2m(n-1), Feige leading term (4/27)n^3, best generic bound, Matthews-type reference, n,m-only OLS reference and constant control, with mean absolute log-ratio error, paired deltas and two-level bootstrap 95% CIs; per-graph Monte Carlo standard errors summarized.
Per-family error table and plot answering how error depends on graph type, with predeclared reliable/fails labels.
Negative-control declarations (made before scoring) and outcomes: permuted-feature (non-vacuity evidence), reordered-copy, constant; any vacuous control reported as such with no causal conclusion.
Reset transcripts matching search [11,12], final [211,212,213] and smoke [11]/[211], RPC counts within 10/15/5/5, and per-episode failures with their worst-case contributions.
Statement that only wall-clock and broker RPC counts were enforced; candidate-internal computation counts were advisory and untrusted; CPU-only allocation per role from harness evidence.

A paper of at most 4 pages in the official ICML LaTeX template (abstract, introduction, method, experiments, discussion and limitations, references), obtained from the official source; if the template cannot be obtained offline this is reported as a blocker, not substituted.
Runnable code with reproduction instructions: environment (Python and numpy/networkx versions), exact commands, all seeds.
Compliance note that the original paper answering this research question, its mirrors, and pages citing or discussing it were not accessed; only the listed starter literature is cited.

Limitations: n <= 30, ten synthetic families, uniform-start expected cover time estimated by Monte Carlo, Feige term is leading-order only, a single candidate from a 1x1 campaign; smoke runs do not attest production results.
